title: Targeting the bile acid receptor TGR5 with Gentiopicroside to activate Nrf2 antioxidant signaling and mitigate Parkinson's disease in an MPTP mouse model.
authors: Gao, Ying; Tang, Xiuling; Yao, Jingyue; Sun, Ting; Chen, Yue; Cheng, Caiyan; Yang, Jingcheng; Wang, Bao; Liu, An; Yang, Le; Zhao, Minggao
one_liner_zh: 该文研究龙胆苦苷靶向TGR5激活Nrf2抗氧化信号缓解帕金森病，核心为小分子-受体互作与神经保护，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a common neurodegenerative disorder characterized by classical symptoms including bradykinesia, rest tremor and rigidity. Oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction are recognized as pivotal factors in PD progression. Gentiopicroside (GPS), a secoiridoid derived from Gentiana manshurica Kitagawa, exhibits antioxidant and mitophagy induction properties. Nonetheless, the effects and mechanisms by which GPS mitigates neurodegeneration in PD remain to be thoroughly elucidated. OBJECTIVES: The goal of this study was to investigate the neuroprotective effects and mechanisms of GPS in PD models. METHODS: We established the MPTP/MPP(+)-induced PD models to measure the neuroprotection of GPS. Transcriptomic analysis, oxidative biochemical kits, western blot and cell immunofluorescence were conducted to elucidate the fundamental mechanisms at play. Subsequently, the targeting and activation of the transmembrane G protein-coupled receptor-5 (TGR5) by GPS were measured by molecular docking, cellular thermal shift assay, microscale thermophoresis (MST) and cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP) quantitation. Finally, we verified whether the neuroprotective and antioxidant effects of GPS were dependent on TGR5 by using specific small interfering RNA (siRNA), pharmacological antagonist and knockout mice. RESULTS: GPS significantly attenuated dopaminergic (DAergic) neuron loss and restored motor function in the MPTP-induced PD mouse model. Whole-genome RNA sequencing and subsequent mechanistic investigations revealed that GPS enhanced the expression and facilitated nuclear entry of factor erythroid-related 2-factor 2 (Nrf2), and reduced oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction stimulated by neurotoxin. Additionally, GPS could target TGR5 and prevent its downregulation in PD model. TGR5's silencing or inhibition weakened the neuroprotective effect of GPS and blocked GPS-mediated activation of Nrf2 antioxidant signaling in PD model. Moreover, the therapeutic effect of GPS in mitigating motor deficits and neurodegeneration was also abolished in Tgr5 knockout mice. CONCLUSION: These findings collectively indicated that GPS targeted TGR5 to activate Nrf2 antioxidant signaling and ultimately ameliorated the pathological progression of PD.
abstract_zh: 引言：帕金森病（Parkinson's disease, PD）是一种常见的神经退行性疾病，其特征性症状包括运动迟缓、静止性震颤和强直。氧化应激和线粒体功能障碍被认为是PD进展中的关键因素。龙胆苦苷（Gentiopicroside, GPS），一种来源于条叶龙胆（Gentiana manshurica Kitagawa）的环烯醚萜苷，具有抗氧化和诱导线粒体自噬的特性。然而，GPS缓解PD中神经退行性变的作用及机制仍需进一步阐明。目的：本研究旨在探讨GPS在PD模型中的神经保护作用及其机制。方法：我们建立了MPTP/MPP(+)诱导的PD模型，以评估GPS的神经保护作用。通过转录组分析、氧化生化试剂盒、蛋白质印迹和细胞免疫荧光实验，阐明其潜在的基本机制。随后，利用分子对接、细胞热位移分析、微量热泳动（MST）和环磷酸腺苷（cAMP）定量测定，评估GPS对跨膜G蛋白偶联受体5（TGR5）的靶向结合及激活作用。最后，通过使用特异性小干扰RNA（siRNA）、药理学拮抗剂和基因敲除小鼠，验证GPS的神经保护和抗氧化效应是否依赖于TGR5。结果：GPS显著减轻了MPTP诱导的PD小鼠模型中多巴胺能（DAergic）神经元丢失，并恢复了运动功能。全基因组RNA测序及后续机制研究显示，GPS增强了核因子E2相关因子2（Nrf2）的表达并促进其核转位，同时减少了神经毒素刺激引起的氧化应激和线粒体功能障碍。此外，GPS能够靶向TGR5，并防止其在PD模型中的下调。TGR5的沉默或抑制削弱了GPS的神经保护作用，并阻断了GPS介导的Nrf2抗氧化信号激活。在Tgr5基因敲除小鼠中，GPS缓解运动缺陷和神经退行性变的治疗效果也被消除。结论：这些发现共同表明，GPS通过靶向TGR5激活Nrf2抗氧化信号，最终改善了PD的病理进展。
